To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a progressive CS architecture based separate sensing of spectral lines and joint reconstruction; (2) we show that this architecture is suitable for onboard acquisition of hyperspectral imagery, by means of a real experiment run on a real satellite.

we propose a novel CS hyperspectral imaging architecture based on separate spatial and spectral sensing and joint spectral-spatial reconstruction; we show that the proposed approach allows to reduce the number of spectral channels by a factor of two, with a slight degradation of the reconstruction quality.

we propose a new architecture for compressive hyperspectral imaging that exploits the progressive acquisition of the spectral channels and that it is based on the joint spatial and spectral Total Variation minimization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new CS architecture suitable for onboard remote acquisition of hyperspectal images, which is based on the joint reconstruction of spectral rows.
the development of novel compressive imaging techniques, which are suitable for remote acquisition, and with the development of new architectures and algorithms for compressive hyperspectral imaging.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach is a promising alternative to existing CS-based solutions, which is able to exploit the strong correlations between spatial and spectral dimensions, allowing to simplify and reduce the complexity of onboard sensors, while maintaining high quality of the reconstructed images.
our approach is the first one to consider a progressive sensing scheme for hyperspectral imaging and to jointly reconstruct the spatial and the spectral information.
the proposed method is a good candidate for onboard hyperspectral imaging, since it is simple and robust.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by using a progressive CS approach, we can achieve a significant reduction of the number of spectral rows to acquire, thus reducing the number of spectral channels to process and, in turn, the complexity of the onboard sensors, while maintaining a comparable performance with respect to standard CS.

the proposed system is a novel CS architecture that exploits the progressive nature of the spectral acquisition of hyperspectral sensors, and the strong spatial and temporal correlations of hyperspectral data, to achieve a significant reduction in the onboard complexity of hyperspectral imaging sensors, while preserving the spatial and spectral information of the original scene.
the progressive CS architecture based upon the joint reconstruction of the spatial and spectral information can achieve the best performance in terms of quality and compression rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a joint reconstruction approach, which exploits the spatial correlations, is more efficient than a decoupled approach, which does not.

progressive CS can be applied to hyperspectral imaging, allowing to reduce the number of spectral channels to be acquired, thus simplifying the architecture of the on-board sensors and reducing the power consumption and data rate.
progressive CS can achieve better results than non-progressive CS in terms of reconstruction quality, while reducing onboard complexity.
